topic_path: CENTRAL REGION PROCEDURES
text:
1. Central – Facility Will Not Provide DWQs

Purpose

This procedure applies when a facility confirms that it does not provide DWQs or Legal Certifications because it issues its own certification.

When to Use

Use this procedure when:

The facility verbally confirms that it does not provide DWQs or Legal Certifications.
Multiple follow-up attempts have already been completed.
The facility advises that its own certification replaces the requested DWQs.

Required Status

Affidavit – No Records – Facility 4th Verbal – Close

Client Note Template

Please note that we received verbal confirmation from [FACILITY] that this facility does not provide any DWQs/Legals, as they provide their own certification.

We have been unable to obtain the DWQs/Legals despite repeated follow-up attempts. Therefore, we are forwarding this order to Client Relations.

If additional information becomes available that may help escalate this request, please let ABI know and we will gladly continue our follow-up.

Facility Name: [FACILITY]

Thank you,

[Name]/[Zone]

Next Action

Send the order to Client Relations.
Document all previous follow-up attempts.
Update the Tracking tab.
2. Final Attempt to Obtain DWQs

Purpose

Use this procedure after the final attempt to obtain missing DWQs or Legal Certifications.

When to Use

Use when:

Records have already been received.
DWQs or Legal Certifications remain outstanding.
Final follow-up has been completed.

Required Status

Affidavit – Of Records Not Secured – Facility 3rd Attempt

Client Note Template

Please be advised that we have received [Record Type] from this facility without the required DWQs/Legals.

We have completed our final follow-up with [Contact Name] at [Phone Number] to obtain the outstanding documentation.

We communicated the urgency of obtaining the required documents; however, no additional updates have been received.

If no response is received, this order will be finalized.

Facility Name: [FACILITY]

Thank you,

[Name]/[Zone]

Next Action

Send the order to Client Relations for closeout approval.
Document the final contact attempt.
3. Central Follow-Up Orders

Purpose

Follow-Up Orders are created when additional action is required after the original work order has been processed.

Purpose

topic_path: 9. Central – Reserves and Re-Service Procedures
text:

topic_path: 9. Central – Reserves and Re-Service Procedures > 9.1 Serve New Address – No Fees
text:

Mail

topic_path: 9. Central – Reserves and Re-Service Procedures > 9.2 Serve New Address – Fees Required

topic_path: 12. Central – Frequently Asked Questions > 12.2 Attorney Satisfactory Letter
text:

What is an Attorney Satisfactory Letter?

Answer

An Attorney Satisfactory Letter is treated the same as an SOA.

For a Deposition SDT, request an authorization signed by the patient.
For a Texas SDT, request a Statement Satisfactory or SOA.

topic_path: 12. Central – Frequently Asked Questions > 12.7 Verify a Duplicate Order
text:
Question

How do we verify whether an order is a duplicate?

Answer

Compare both orders and confirm:

Patient name
Date of birth
Social Security number
Facility information
Dates of service
Requested record types
Customer or client name

Treat the order as a duplicate only when the relevant information matches.

topic: 12.8 Void and Reissue an Uncashed Check

display_title: 12.8 Void and Reissue an Uncashed Check
header: 12.8 Void and Reissue an Uncashed Check
text:
Question

When should a check be voided?

Answer

If a check was issued more than four weeks ago and has not been cashed:

Contact the SP Check Team.
Ask them to void the original payment.
Request that the internal team reissue the check.
Document the request and follow-up.

topic: 12.9 Email or Written Confirmation as ANR
topic_path: 12. Central – Frequently Asked Questions > 12.9 Email or Written Confirmation as ANR
display_title: 12.9 Email or Written Confirmation as ANR
header: 12.9 Email or Written Confirmation as ANR
text:
Question

Can email or written confirmation be accepted as an ANR?

Answer

Medical Authorization Request

Email or written confirmation may be accepted as an ANR.

Print the email or written confirmation as a PDF.
Upload it as correspondence.
Send the order for ANR review.

Subpoena Request

Email or written confirmation is not sufficient.

A DWQ or ANR must be obtained before the order can be closed.

How can we verify whether a check was cashed?

Send the order number to your immediate supervisor and ask them to verify the check status.

topic: 12.12 Use an Existing ANR for a Follow-Up X-Ray Order
topic_path: 12. Central – Frequently Asked Questions > 12.12 Use an Existing ANR for a Follow-Up X-Ray Order
display_title: 12.12 Use an Existing ANR for a Follow-Up X-Ray Order
header: 12.12 Use an Existing ANR for a Follow-Up X-Ray Order
text:
Question

Can an ANR from the original order be used to close a follow-up X-ray order?

Answer

Yes, the ANR from the original order may be used if it includes the required information, such as:

Correct patient information
Applicable facility information
Requested record type

Confirm that the ANR applies to the follow-up order before closing it.

topic_path: 12. Central – Frequently Asked Questions > 12.13 Out-of-Country Facility Cannot Be Contacted
text:
Question

What should we do when a facility is outside the United States and cannot be contacted?

Answer

Document all contact and research attempts in the Tracking notes.
Include available address and contact information.
Send the order to the Client Relations queue.
Request further assistance from the client.

topic: 12.14 Request Address Does Not Match Authorization Address
topic_path: 12. Central – Frequently Asked Questions > 12.14 Request Address Does Not Match Authorization Address
display_title: 12.14 Request Address Does Not Match Authorization Address
header: 12.14 Request Address Does Not Match Authorization Address
text:
Question

Can the request cover page be updated when its address does not match the authorization?

Answer

Yes.

Send the order number to your immediate supervisor and request a new cover page using the address listed on the authorization.

Do not alter the executed authorization.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK
text:
1. Basic Functions of MR8

Purpose

The three most commonly used MR8 functions are:

Case Manager
Calling Cards
Task Manager

These functions help users search for cases, review facility and patient information, manage assigned calls, and document actions taken.

How to Open MR8 Functions

Open Case Manager

Select the Orders tab.
Select Case Manager.
Alternatively, press the F2 key.

Open Task Manager

Select Task Manager from the dropdown below Case Manager.

Open Using Icons

Click the corresponding Case Manager or Task Manager icon.

2. Case Manager

Purpose

Case Manager is the primary search function in MR8. Use it to search for:

Cases
Patients
Orders
Facilities
Records
Client information

Case Manager Screen Layout

Top Half — Case Shell: Displays case-specific and client information.
Bottom Half — Parts: Displays all facilities to which a request has been sent for the selected case.
Left Pane — Search Criteria: Contains the fields used to search for cases and orders.

Best Ways to Search

The recommended search methods are:

Order number
Patient name under Records Of

Troubleshooting Search Results

If you are unable to find the correct result:

Click the Clear All Search Criteria icon in the bottom-left corner.
Re-enter or refresh the search criteria.
Search using only part of the patient's name.

Important Name Search Rules

Patient names must match the format entered in MR8.
A search for Jane Doe may not return results if the patient is entered as Jane C. Doe.
Search using only Jane or Doe when the complete name does not return a result.

Order Number and Part Number

Table:
Type | Format | Example | Description
Order Number | 12345 | 12345 | Case-specific number assigned when the case is created
Part Number | 12345.001 | 001 | Identifies a specific facility or location within the case

Open a Calling Card from Case Manager

Double-click any item listed under Parts to open its Calling Card.

3. Calling Cards

Purpose

A Calling Card contains the information and activity associated with a specific facility or part of an order.

Double-click a part in Case Manager to open its Calling Card.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.1 General Tab
text:
The General tab displays:

Facility information
Patient information
Record types requested from the facility
The View Case Info option for additional case-level information

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.2 Additional Info Tab
text:
Remarks Section

The Remarks section contains specific instructions related to the records requested, including:

Dates of service
Specific studies requested by the client
Additional record specifications
Special handling instructions

Always review the Remarks section before contacting the facility.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.3 Tracking Tab
text:
Purpose

The Tracking tab contains the complete history of actions taken on a part.

Common Tracking Steps

Called Custodian: Use when calling the facility.
Emailed Request: Use when emailing the request to the facility.

Important Compliance Note

All clients can view published tracking steps. Enter only accurate, clear, and professional information in the Remarks field.

Enter a New Tracking Step

Click Change Step.
Select or enter the action taken under Next Step.
Do not change the Step Due Date.
Do not change the Publish checkbox.
Enter a concise summary of the action in Remarks.
Click OK.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.4 Services Tab
text:
Purpose

Use the Services tab to document or request additional billable services.

Common services include:

FedEx
Certified mail
UPS
Courier
Hand service or Service of Process

Add a Service

Click New.
Search for the required service under Service Item.
Select the correct service.

Example: FedEx Ground Charge

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.5 Fee Checks Tab
text:
Purpose

Use the Fee Checks tab to:

Request payment for an invoice.
Verify whether a check has already been issued.
Review payment details.

Information Displayed for an Issued Check

Check date
Check number
Check amount

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.6 Notes Log Tab
text:
Purpose

The Notes Log is a temporary working area used while speaking with a facility.

It allows users to:

Document information during a call.
Review other Calling Card tabs while typing.
Prepare a complete note before entering a tracking step.

Difference Between Notes Log and Tracking Step

When a new Notes Log entry is open, you can navigate between other tabs.
When a Tracking Step window is open, you cannot navigate to other tabs until it is closed.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.7 Part-Level Repository Tab
text:
Purpose

The Part-Level Repository contains documents associated with a specific facility or part, including:

Assembled requests
Subpoenas
Authorizations
Invoices
Documents used for resubmission

Find the Correct Request for Resubmission

Locate Copy of Subpoena/Authorization.
Review the Upload Date.
Select the document with the upload date closest to the current date.

The most recently uploaded request is generally the most current or revised request packet.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 3.8 Records Of Tab
text:
Purpose

The Records Of tab contains patient contact information.

It may display:

Patient address
Patient phone number
Patient email address
4. Task Manager

Purpose

Task Manager is used to access and manage calls assigned to the user.

Task Manager Search Criteria

Table:
Field | Required Setting
Assign To | Select your name
Action Date From | Set the date back several years
Action Date To | Set the date forward several years
Group By Box | Enable filterable column headings

Find Your Name

Click the Binoculars icon.
Enter your name in the Display Name field.
Click Search.
Select your name.

Configure the View

Click View above the Search Criteria section.
Confirm that Group By Box is selected.

Work the Call List

Work from the top of the list to the bottom.
Start with the oldest action date.
Review the total number of assigned calls at the bottom of the list.
Complete a full cycle of assigned calls within 14 business days.
Contact at least 80 facilities per day through phone, fax, mail, or email.

Primary Objective

The primary objective is to obtain the requested records.

Consistent facility follow-up increases the likelihood of receiving records promptly.

Daily Call List Review

At the beginning of each day:

Record the number of calls assigned to you.
Work the calls in action-date order.
Monitor the call count as records are received and calls are completed.

Locate Legal Requests

Every assigned call has a corresponding legal request.

Requests can be found in:

Case-Level Repository: Contains raw case documents.
Part-Level Repository: Contains the assembled legal request for the specific facility.
5. Additional MR8 Functions

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 5.1 Turn In
text:
Purpose

Turn In is the MR8 repository used for received documents, including:

Records
Letters
Film breakdowns
Fee approvals
Invoices
Other received correspondence

Open Turn In

Right-click any call in Case Manager or Task Manager.
Select Turn In.

Important Research Tip

Use previously received documents to verify conflicting information such as:

Date of birth
Social Security number
Facility phone number
Facility contact information

If a facility cannot be located but a letter was previously received, review the letter for updated contact information.

Turn In Screen

The Turn In window contains four boxes labeled Step 1 through Step 4.

Callers should review only Step 1. Steps 2 through 4 are handled by billing.

View a Turn In File

Double-click the item under Step 1.
The Received Record window will open.
Navigate to the Item-Level Repository.
Click View File.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 5.2 Firms Tab
text:
Purpose

Use the Firms tab to locate information about a client's law firm, including:

Phone number
Address
Fax number
Email addresses

6. Types of Requests

Purpose

This section explains where legal request documents are stored, the difference between subpoenas and authorizations, and the departments responsible for different record types.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 6.1 Case-Level Repository
text:
Purpose

The Case-Level Repository contains important documents associated with the complete case.

Documents Available in the Case-Level Repository

The repository may contain:

Subpoenas
Authorizations
Letters of Administration
Powers of Attorney
Birth certificates
Death certificates
Other supporting case documents

Access the Case-Level Repository

Option 1: Through Case Manager

Open Case Manager.
Open the applicable Case Shell.
Select the Case-Level Repository tab.

Option 2: Through a Calling Card

Open the applicable Calling Card.
Click View Case Info.
Open the Case-Level Repository.

Important Request Assembly Rule

Documents pulled from the Case-Level Repository are raw case documents.

Before sending them to a facility, assemble the complete request packet and confirm that all required supporting documents are included.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 6.2 Types of Legal Requests
text:
Subpoena

A subpoena is a legal writ generally issued through a court or government authority to compel testimony or the production of evidence.

Key features:

Usually signed by an attorney or judge.
Requires the facility to provide a response.
Failure to comply may result in legal consequences.

Authorization

An authorization is a medical release signed by the patient that permits the release of records to the requesting law firm.

Key features:

Must be signed by the patient or an authorized representative.
Records may occasionally be released directly to Choice Legal.

topic: 6.3 Route Requests to the Correct Department
topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 6.3 Route Requests to the Correct Department

Record Type | Department

Alternative Names for Medical Records Departments

Release of Information
ROI
Health Information Management
HIM
7. Record Types

Purpose

This section identifies common record types and explains where to review client-specific requirements.

Record types are listed on the General tab of the Calling Card.

Common Record Types

Table:
Record Type | Description | Important Notes
Medical, billing, and films | The most common combination of requested records | The request may include any combination of these record types
Insurance | Health, automobile, or other insurance records | Facilities generally respond to subpoenas; review Remarks for the claim number
Cell phone | Cell phone usage or account records | Review Remarks for the applicable phone number and time frame
Employment | Records from a current or previous employer | Request the complete employment file unless otherwise specified
Medicaid or Medicare | Claim-related government benefit records | Requirements depend on the specific claim
Paramedic | Emergency medical service records | Billing records are generally required; requests may be handled through Chartswap
Optical | Eye-care records | Billing is generally required; imaging may be included
Dental | Dental records | Billing is generally required; X-rays may be included

Review Additional Information and Remarks

Before contacting a facility, review:

Additional Info → Remarks

The Remarks section may specify:

Dates of service
Particular studies
Specific record types
Special client instructions
Whether the client wants any and all records

When Remarks Are Blank

If the request is for medical records and the Remarks section does not specify a limited date range or specific records, request any and all medical records.

8. Statuses and Color Codes

Purpose

Calling Cards and locations are color-coded to show their current status, urgency, and required follow-up frequency.

Status and Color Guide

Table:
Color | Status | Description | Required Follow-Up
Black | In Progress | New or active calls that are not Rush or Pilot | Every 14 business days
Red | Rush/In Progress | Expedited request for any client | Every 4 business days
Pink | Pilot/In Progress | Newer or Pilot client request | Every 4 business days
Maroon and Mustard | Liberty TN/PEAK | Liberty Tennessee or PEAK request | Follow the Black-status schedule unless otherwise instructed
Brick and Soft Pink | NickasKehoe | NK and NK Rush requests | Follow the applicable NK procedure
Green | Records Obtained | Records or another item have been uploaded to Turn In | Generally complete; verify whether further action is required
Orange | Objected To | At least one party has objected to the subpoena | Not on call list; email a closer
Purple | Cancelled | Request cancelled for reasons such as new counsel | Not on call list; email a closer when required
Blue | Settled | The case has settled | Not on call list
Light Blue | Non-Vendor Case | Opposing counsel objected or the request was sent directly by an attorney | Follow up with the client
Mint | Waiting for Signed Authorization or Subpoena | Facility will not respond to the existing request and additional client documentation is required | Email the client for assistance or permission

Purpose

The primary objective of facility contact is to obtain the requested records or determine the exact action required to move the request forward.

Work the Call List

Start with the oldest action date.
Work from the top of the call list to the bottom.

Select the appropriate contact method based on the request history.

Custodian’s first name
Initial of the custodian’s last name
Custodian’s phone number

Records@ChoiceLegal.com

PRI Response Letter

The facility is unable to provide the requested records.
The client instructs Choice Legal to close the request.

Response Letter Rules

Table:
Client | Rejection Letter Received | No Rejection Letter | Duplicate Location
PRI | Email the client and forward the request to Kari or Ashleigh for closure | Email the client, create the response letter, and send it to Records@ChoiceLegal.com | Create a duplicate notice letter and send it to Records@ChoiceLegal.com
ExamWorks | Email Kari or Ashleigh for closure | Create the response letter and send it to Records@ChoiceLegal.com | Create a duplicate notice letter and send it to Records@ChoiceLegal.com

Key Difference Between PRI and ExamWorks

For PRI, email the client when required.
For ExamWorks, do not email the client unless specifically instructed.

12. Fee Approvals

Purpose

Fee Approval is required when a facility’s invoice exceeds the client’s approved fee threshold.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 12.1 Client Fee Threshold
text:
Choice Legal may pay facility fees that fall below the client’s approved threshold.

Example:

If the client’s threshold is $300.00, Choice Legal may process fees up to $299.99 without requesting additional approval.

Any amount equal to or greater than the threshold requires client approval.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 12.2 Fee Approval Process
text:
The Films Department sends the invoice to the client.
The client is advised of the total fee amount.
The client reviews the invoice.
The client either approves or denies the fee.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 12.3 When the Fee Is Approved
text:
If the client approves the fee:

The Films Department requests payment.
The applicable check or payment process is started.
The order remains active until the records are received or further instructions are provided.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 12.4 When the Fee Is Denied
text:
If the client denies the fee:

The call may be removed from the call list.
Follow the applicable closure process.

For PRI or ExamWorks requests, a response letter may be required before closing the location.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 12.5 Fee Approval Follow-Up Schedule
text:
Fee Approval requests are followed up three times over three months.

First attempt: Initial Fee Approval email
Second attempt: Approximately 30 days after the first attempt
Third attempt: Approximately 30 days after the second attempt

If the previous email was sent more than 30 days ago, request the next follow-up attempt.

Example:

Please send Fee Approval attempt 2 of 3.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 12.6 Organize Fee Approval Emails
text:
Create a dedicated email subfolder for Fee Approval correspondence.

Use the folder to track:

Initial approval requests
Second attempts
Third attempts
Client approvals
Client denials

A Film Breakdown provides detailed information about available films or imaging studies so the client can review and approve the related duplication fee.

topic: 13.1 Information Included in a Film Breakdown
topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 13.1 Information Included in a Film Breakdown

text:

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 13.3 Film Breakdown Follow-Up Schedule
text:
Follow up three times over three months.

First attempt: Initial Film Breakdown email
Second attempt: Approximately 30 days later
Third attempt: Approximately 30 days after the second attempt

If no response is received after the required attempts, the location may be eligible for closure according to the applicable client procedure.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 13.4 Identify a Possible Duplicate Location
text:
A duplicate location may exist when a facility states:

The records were already sent.
The records were included with another request.
Another facility or physician is part of the same office.
The same records were previously provided under another order.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 13.5 Verify a Duplicate Location
text:
Review the facility information on both orders.
Compare the patient information.
Compare the requested record types.
Compare the dates of service.
Contact the facilities involved.
Confirm whether the physicians work at the same office.
Confirm whether the records for both requests were included in one response.
Follow the duplicate-location procedure if the information matches.

16. PRI Codefendants

Purpose

PRI Codefendant cases occur when multiple PRI law firms request records for the same patient from the same facility.

These cases are an exception to the general rule of one case shell per patient.

topic_path: CHOICE LEGAL CALLER'S TASKBOOK > 16.1 Identify PRI Codefendant Cases
text:
PRI Codefendant cases may include:

Multiple case shells for the same patient
Different PRI law firms
The same facility
The same or overlapping requested records

19. Copy Companies

text:

The legal request is sent to the healthcare facility.

The copy company processes the request, invoices (if applicable), and releases the records.

20. Example Call Scenarios

Purpose

The following examples demonstrate recommended conversations for common retrieval scenarios. Use these examples as guidance while following the applicable SOP.

Scenario 1 – Records Already Mailed

Situation

The facility confirms that the requested records have already been mailed.

Recommended Conversation

Caller

Good afternoon. My name is [Your Name], and I am calling from Choice Legal regarding a records request for [Patient Name].

Facility

The request was received last week, and the medical and billing records were mailed yesterday.

Caller

Thank you. May I confirm whether any radiology films are available?

Facility

No. We do not maintain films at this office.

Caller

Thank you. May I have your first name and the initial of your last name for documentation purposes?

Required Actions

Confirm all requested record types.
Ask whether any additional records remain outstanding.
Record the custodian's name.
Document the tracking step.
Continue or close follow-up according to the applicable SOP.

Scenario 2 – Facility Requests the Records Request to Be Resent

Situation

The facility cannot locate the request and asks that it be resent.

Recommended Conversation

Caller

Good afternoon. My name is [Your Name] from Choice Legal. I am calling regarding a subpoena that was previously sent for [Patient Name].

Facility

I do not see the request in our system. Could you resend it?

Caller

Certainly. Could you please confirm the correct fax number or email address for Medical Records?

Facility

Our fax number is 813-123-4567.

Caller

Thank you. I will resend the request today and follow up next week.

Required Actions

Verify the fax number or email address.
Resend the most recent request packet.
Update the Tracking tab.
Schedule the next follow-up.

Scenario 3 – Facility Requires a Patient Authorization

Situation

The facility refuses to release records because an executed patient authorization is required.

Recommended Conversation

Facility

The request was denied because the file contains sensitive information, and we require a signed patient authorization.

Caller

Thank you. I will notify the client and obtain the required authorization. Once received, may I send it to the same department?

Facility

Yes. Please send it by certified mail to our physical address.

Required Actions

Determine why the request was denied.
Identify the required documentation.
Notify Client Relations.
Attach the rejection letter.
Update the Tracking tab.

Scenario 4 – Out-of-State Subpoena Has No Jurisdiction

Situation

The facility advises that the subpoena cannot be honored because it has no legal jurisdiction.

Recommended Conversation

Facility

Your subpoena has no jurisdiction because it was issued out of state.

Caller

Thank you. I will request a signed patient authorization and submit it as soon as it is received. May I confirm the appropriate fax number or email address?

Required Actions

Confirm that the request requires a patient authorization.
Verify the correct delivery method.
Notify Client Relations.
Document the conversation.
Schedule the next follow-up.

topic_path: 1. Hartford Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.10 Call Flow Helpful Tips
text:
Pre Call:

1. Review the order
a. Status history and uploaded documents.
i. If follow up, review original to ensure we did not receive what is being requested on the follow up or alt. contact information (notes or records received)
b. Review the type of records requested.
i. If Subpoena, affidavit
ii. If Texas Civil Subpoena, DWQs
c. Subpoena Phrase for specific claim, DOS, etc.
d. Days request has been open.
e. If a payment has been issued, when, and has it been cashed.
f. Any numbers, emails, faxes we have tried and have been successful receiving a response.
g. The number of attempts have we made.
h. Any notices that have or have not been sent.
2. Know your objective
a. Is this a status check
b. Confirmation of receipt of request
c. Confirmation of receipt of payment
d. Escalation delay
e. Firm completion date
3. Prepare your ask
a. "Can you confirm when the records will be completed?"
b. "What is preventing the release of records at this time?
c. "What is the exact turnaround time from today?"
4. Documentation ready
a. Have all information readily available to reduce time spent on the call

During Call:

1. Strong opening
a. "Hello, this is (NAME) calling from ABI Document Support Services regarding a records request for (RECORD TYPES). Are you the best point of contact for these records or you able to provide the best point of contact for these records?"

***Confident and friendly tone = faster cooperation***

2. Verify key milestones – Ask clearly – if Applicable
a. Did you receive the request? (Confirm WO)
b. Is it valid and complete to your facility's policy?
c. Is the phone, fax, email, address we have on file correct?
d. Are fees required?
e. Has the request been processed? (Confirm WO and Record Types)
f. If not, where is it in the queue?
g. What is the expected completion date?
h. Can you send to me directly to ensure quicker processing?
i. West Region - California location addresses: Can we pay and pick up? Can we pick up? Can we Copy?
j. Central Region - Texas location addresses: Can we pay and pick up? Can we pick up? Can we Copy?

***Never hang up without a date or clear next step***

3. Handle delays with urgency
a. "Its in process"  "What is the estimated completion date?"
b. "Were behind"  "What is the earliest realistic release date?"
c. "We don't have it"  "Can I resend it while I have you on the call?

***Push politely (assertive, yet professional). Always obtain a timeline. Use prior conversations and dates to your advantage***

4. Confirm before ending
a. "Just to confirm, (XYZ) will be completed by __ and sent via __?"
5. Professional close
a. "Thank you for your assistance. We will follow up on __ if no response has been received."

Post Call:

1. Detailed notes – Aka Audit Criteria (Avoid $ amounts, specific emails, faxes, names, dates, etc. and other WOs not pertaining to that record subject)
a. Name of custodian
b. Direct phone/fax/email
c. Record types (affidavit/DWQ if required)
d. Exact status
e. Any barriers
2. Ask teammates or leadership if they have any helpful information on this facility

***Future you, teammates, client, CR, etc should not need to guess what your notes mean***

3. Immediate action items
a. Resend request? (Ensure all required items are included: Auth, Subpoena, LOR, etc.)
b. Send Notice?
c. Follow up internally?
d. Send order to CR? (Ensure we do not already have in Attachments, Print Single Models, or other orders where we have received records)

Urgency mindset:

1. Every call ends with a date
2. Every delay gets a valid reason
3. Every note tells a story of the call
4. Everything is done 100% before moving on to next order

header: 1.13 Client Relations – Record Retrieval and Record Retrieval – Client Relations
text:
Client Relations and Customer Service are interchangeable terms for the department that handles our Clients directly and their concerns. Any time that we need more information or need to report an issue that we've run into that we cannot fix in our own department, we notify Client Relations for further review/ assistance.

The flow of information must be passed within the Retrieval and Client Relations departments. The Custodian/ Facility will never speak to Client Relations directly just as Retrieval will never speak to the Client directly. In order for the communication to stay open both Retrieval and Client Relations must relay the information being requested from the Custodian/ Facility and the Client.

There are only certain occasions where the Custodian/ Facility and the Client will get in contact with each other. Such as, the Custodian/ Facility may want more details on the case (which ABI does not have), to clarify the information being requested on the subpoena/ authorization or if they refuse to speak with ABI regarding a concern. Our Client may also contact the Facility directly if they are being non-compliant and we request for them to intervene.

topic_path: 1. Hartford Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.15 Email Etiquette for Professional Workplaces
text:
With the sheer volume of emails that we read and write each day, we may be more prone to making errors and those errors can have professional consequences. Here are important tips you need to know when writing an email in your professional environment.

Include a clear, direct subject line. People often decide whether to open an email based on the subject line. Good subject lines give the reader a preview of what the email is about.

Begin each email with a greeting: No matter how pressed for time you are, a simple greeting such as "Hi," "Hello," or "Dear" is good etiquette. Otherwise, if you launch into your email without a greeting or introduction you run the risk of seeming impolite or impatient.

End emails in a friendly way: Use ending such as "Best wishes" or "Have a great day". Even if you use the same ending with everyone, it ends the email in a warm and positive way.

Think twice before hitting Reply All. No one wants to read emails from 20 people that have nothing to do with them. Refrain from hitting Reply All unless you really think everyone on the list needs to receive the email.

Include a signature block. Provide your reader with some information about you, such as your full name, title, the organization name, and your contact information, including a phone number. Use the same font, type size, and color as the rest of the email.

Be cautious with humour. Humour can easily get lost in translation without the right tone or facial expressions. In a professional exchange, it is better to leave humour out of emails unless you know the recipient well.

Proofread every message. Ensure you are using correct spelling and proper grammar. Your mistakes will be noticed by the recipients and you may be judged for making them. Do not rely on spell-checkers. Read and reread your email, preferably aloud, before sending it.

Add the email address last. This prevents you from sending an email accidentally before you have finished writing and proofing the message. Even when you are replying to a message, it's a good precaution to delete the recipient's address and insert it only when you are sure the message is ready to be sent.

Double-check that you have selected the correct recipient. Pay careful attention when typing a name on the email's "To" line. It is easy to select the wrong name and this could cause a breach of privacy, embarrassment, or wasted time.

Keep your fonts classic. The ideal font is Arial, size 12 in black. Your emails should be easy for other people to read.

Keep tabs on your tone. Tone is easy to misconstrue without the context from vocal cues and facial expressions. It's easy to appear more abrupt than you intended. Avoid using negative words ("failure," "wrong," "neglected"), and use "please" and "thank you." To avoid misunderstandings, read your message out loud before sending.

Nothing is confidential--so write accordingly. A basic guideline is to assume that others will see what you write. Don't write anything that would be ruinous to you or hurtful to others. After all, work email is owned by your organization and email is easy to forward.

Use threads: if you get a message from someone and you are going to respond, don't send a new message, simply hit the reply option on your email, this keeps the original subject line with "Re:" in front of it.

Protect addresses: If you are sending out an email to a large private list use BCC: (blind carbon copy), don't use CC: (carbon copy) to protect the addresses of the recipients.

Be concise: Get to the point of your email as quickly as possible, but don't leave out important details that will help your recipient answer your query.

Do not use all CAPS in your emails: This is perceived as yelling in the digital world. If you need to emphasize something, use bold or italics on the points you want to emphasize.

If you are sending an email with an attachment, make mention of it in the body of the email: Write in the email that you are sending an attachment so that the reader knows there is more to the email than just the text.

Use an Auto-responder: When you're away from the office and not available for an extended time, set an auto-responder to automatically reply to emails. Include the email of another colleague for emergencies. This lets people know when to expect a response and who to contact if a response is required sooner.

Don't send an email when you are emotional or angry. Wait for 24 hours before writing your response or hitting send.

topic_path: 1. Hartford Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.22 Non-Compliance Process
text:
Question

What is the Hartford Region process for marking an order non-compliant?

Procedure

A facility is considered "non-compliant" when the due/ deposition date has passed. The facility may have stated that records have been in process for weeks without a valid explanation or if you have not had any valid contact with the facility. Ensure that the below due diligence has been applied and followed.

1. Read all the notes for important/maybe different contact info.
2. Attempt all numbers in profile (even if it's not for the record type you are following up for)
3. Attempt all options, not just for the dept. for the record type we are following up for.
4. Ask for a manager!
a. If manager is not available.
i. When will they be in?
ii. Do they have a direct number, email, and fax?
iii. Who is their boss?
iv. Is the doctor available?
5. Check other orders for that facility for alt. contact info.
6. Google for alt. contact (send a fax/email on top of making phone calls to the facility)
7. Check for duplicates
8. Send appropriate non-compliant notices. (Follow the SOPs)

When leaving messages, you must express the upmost urgency. Advise how many calls we have made, the due date, the non-compliance notices we have sent, the lack of response, if a response is not received the client may petition a Motion to Compel, as well as request an immediate call back from the manager that day!

*You must note ALL of your efforts*

topic_path: 1. Hartford Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.27 Solcom Fix - QC Codes
text:
When handing in the fix basket, you should be reviewing the notes in Solcom not Wincopy to identify why it was returned. There will be 1 of 2 things listed for your return.

1. There should be a detailed description from QC or Lead indicating what is needed.
2. If there is no detailed description, there should be a QC# code. Each number stands for something.

QC1- Order is already closed and billed. Something was uploaded to the order after it was closed. You need to see what was uploaded and identify if you need to create a follow up and have the items moved to the follow up order or verify if they are duplicate and let us know if we need to disregard.

QC2- The order is missing a status letter for your closeout, or it’s missing an affidavit of records or of no records. You will need to identify which one based on how it was closed and what's present and not present in Solcom.

QC3- Records are not showing in Solcom, therefore you need to re-upload them. This could be of system issues or may have dropped them incorrectly.

QC4- You need to verify records are correct. This means either the name, date of birth, or facility name does not match what the client provided on the order. You need to verify if they are correct. If they are you need to enter a note for QC that its ok to process records as you verified they are correct.

QC5- The incorrect status letter format was uploaded, wrong affidavit, or you need a status letter because the custodian filled out the affidavit incorrectly, meaning they signed it on the wrong spot, or they marked something was not provided when in fact it was provided.

QC6- There is an invoice in Solcom on this order showing as unpaid. You need to verify if it needs to be paid and move forward with the process of issuing payment. Once payment is issued your leads can move the order back to QC.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > 2.2 Central - Follow Up Orders
text:
Question

What are follow up orders and how should they be handled?

Follow ups are orders that are created from original orders. Follow ups may be created by Client Relations or Clerical Support to either obtain records that were not originally provided or to challenge a CNR. Follow ups from Client Relations need more diligence as we either, already received records but maybe missing some necessary documents or if the client has provided proof that records do exist after we already obtained a CNR. Follow ups from Clerical Support are orders that you request personally such as a Bcopy, Xcopy or for the signed affidavit.

· Bcopy: Specifically created for billing records

· Xcopy: Specifically created for digital imaging ONLY, if they exist at the facility

· Follow up for missing records: Created by Client Relations as the Client believes not all records were provided or if specific information is missing

· Follow up for missing Affidavit of Custodian of Records: Created by Clerical Support to continue following up for the missing affidavit as records were previously provided without

· Follow up to challenge CNR: Created by Client Relations if the Client provides some form of proof that records exist or if they provide additional information that may help the facility locate records

· Follow up for additional fees: Created by your Lead or Supervisor as records were already received and processed but we failed to pay the fees before we closed the order. These should be sent to your Lead or Supervisor to review and have fees issued and order closed

*** If an order is a M/B/X or M/X and an invoice or breakdown for the xrays is received, a follow up order will need to be requested and marked as high importance for an Xcopy as Xrays must be their own order. Email is TexusFU@abidss.com ***

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > 2.10 Central - Scheduling
text:
Question

What is the scheduling process?

If records are ready to be picked up or copied, or a notary is needed. Make sure you ask all of the questions below completely as your driver does not have Wincopy to verify information. If an appointment is necessary, request at least a two-hour window as your driver may run into traffic or have trouble finding parking and ask for a back-up date/time in case the first option is not available.

VERIFY YOUR INFORMATION

· Are we picking up or copying? (THIS MAKES A BIG DIFFERENCE IN THE DRIVER'S TRIP)

- If copy, verify how many inches so that your driver has an idea on how long it will take

(Generally, 1 inch can take anywhere from 20-30 minutes)

· What are the days and hours our driver can go? (Ex: M-F 8-12/1-5; Tues & Thurs 8-12; Fridays Only 8-5) -Is a specific appointment necessary, if so follow the above instructions

· If the order is requesting billing records, Is billing included?

-If yes, make sure to list it (Ex: medical and billing records)

-If no, the facility needs to provide an explanation on the Affidavit as to why they do not have billing or where else it can be obtained from

· If the order is requesting Xrays, does their office do any imaging in-house?

-If no, use the VPU/VTC status with "NO FILMS"

-If yes, verify if we are obtaining a breakdown and you will need to request an Xcopy

· Do we owe the facility any fees for their services?

-How much and who do we make the check payable to?

· Verify the address that we are picking up/ copying from

Steps Once the Above is Complete

- Status the order accordingly depending on what is needed or being obtained
- Email RPersaud@abidss.com and BErwin@abidss.com with the information above

What are follow up orders and how should they be handled in the West region?

Follow ups are orders that are created from original orders. Follow ups may be created by Client Relations or Clerical Support to either obtain records that were not originally provided or to challenge a CNR. Follow ups from Client Relations need more diligence as we either, already received records but maybe missing some necessary documents or if the client has provided proof that records do exist after we already obtained a CNR. Follow ups from Clerical Support are orders that you request personally such as a Bcopy, Xcopy or for the signed affidavit.

· Bcopy: Specifically created for billing records

· Xcopy: Specifically created for digital imaging ONLY, if they exist at the facility

· Follow up for missing records: Created by Client Relations as the Client believes not all records were provided or if specific information is missing

· Follow up for missing Affidavit of Custodian of Records: Created by Clerical Support to continue following up for the missing affidavit as records were previously provided without

· Follow up to challenge CNR: Created by Client Relations if the Client provides some form of proof that records exist or if they provide additional information that may help the facility locate records

· Follow up for additional fees: Created by your Lead or Supervisor as records were already received and processed but we failed to pay the fees before we closed the order. These should be sent to your Lead or Supervisor to review and have fees issued and order closed

*** If an order is a M/B/X or M/X and an invoice or breakdown for the xrays is received, a follow up order will need to be requested and marked as high importance for an Xcopy as Xrays must be their own order. Email is ABIRDRouteFOLLOWUPS@abidss.com ***

text:
Question

What is the scheduling process in the West region for California only?

If records are ready to be picked up or copied, schedule accordingly. Make sure you ask all of the questions below completely as your driver does not have Wincopy to verify information. If an appointment is necessary, request at least a two-hour window as your driver may run into traffic or have trouble finding parking and ask for a back-up date/time in case the first option is not available. But before you schedule, you must first reach out to the Field Department Management Team to confirm if there will be a driver available.

VERIFY YOUR INFORMATION

· Are we picking up or copying? (THIS MAKES A BIG DIFFERENCE IN THE DRIVER'S TRIP)

- If copy, verify how many inches so that your driver has an idea on how long it will take

(Generally, 1 inch can take anywhere from 20-30 minutes)

· What are the days and hours our driver can go? (Ex: M-F 8-12/1-5; Tues & Thurs 8-12; Fridays Only 8-5) -Is a specific appointment necessary, if so follow the above instructions

· If the order is requesting billing records, Is billing included?

-If yes, make sure to list it (Ex: medical and billing records)

-If no, the facility needs to provide an explanation on the Affidavit as to why they do not have billing or where else it can be obtained from

· If the order is requesting Xrays, does their office do any imaging in-house?

-If no, use the VPU/VTC status with "NO FILMS"

-If yes, verify if we are obtaining a breakdown and you will need to request an Xcopy

· Do we owe the facility any fees for their services?

-How much and who do we make the check payable to?

· Verify the address that we are picking up/ copying from

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > HIPAA COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST - AUTHORIZATION
text:
INFORMATION 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(i) A description of the information to be disclosed that identifies the information in a specific and meaningful fashion.

DISCLOSING ENTITY 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(ii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, authorized to make the disclosure.

RECIPIENT 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(iii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, to whom the covered entity may make the requested disclosure.

PURPOSE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(iv) A description of each purpose of the requested use or disclosure. The statement "at the request of the individual" is a sufficient description of the purpose when an individual initiates the authorization an does not, or elects not to, provide a statement of the purpose.

EXPIRATION DATE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(v) An expiration date or an expiration event that relates to the use or disclosure.

SIGNATURE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(vi) Signature of the individual and date. A copy of a signature is sufficient if the document states "a copy shall be considered as original".

RIGHT TO REVOKE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(2)(i) The exceptions to the right to revoke and a description of how the individual may revoke the authorization.

NO CONDITIONS 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(2)(ii) The covered entity may not condition treatment, payment, enrolment or eligibility for benefits on whether the individual signs the authorization.

POTENTIAL FOR REDISCLOSURE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(2)(iii) The potential for information disclosed pursuant to the authorization to be subject to redisclosure by the recipient and no longer protected.

PLAIN LANGUAGE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(3) Authorization is written in plain language.

COPY TO INDIVIDUAL 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(4) If a covered entity seeks an authorization from an

individual for use or disclosure of protected health information, the covered entity must provide

the individual with a copy of the signed authorization. This is not applicable to copy services

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > TYPES OF REQUESTS
text:
The Scheduling Department handles all types of requests and each one differs from the other. Though

they are all requests for the same type of records and/or facilities, we must handle each one differently.

See below for definitions:

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > SIGNED AUTHORIZATION
text: An authorization is a request in which the record subject/patient has signed a request giving our office permission to obtain a copy of their records. Authorizations must comply with state and federal HIPAA requirements.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > DEPOSITION SUBPOENA
text: A Deposition Subpoena is a request for records. By law, the subpoena provides a maximum of 15 days from the date of service for the facility to comply. Records obtained from any facility with this type of request will always require that an affidavit be accompanied indicating whether they have records or not. Federal, Out-of-State, requests for "sensitive" records, and Native American locations are not bound by California subpoenas as the request either lacks sufficient authority or there is no jurisdiction.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > WORKERS COMPENSATION SUBPOENA
text: This type of request allows for a maximum of 10 days to comply from the date served.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > PHOTOCOPY SPECIAL
text: There are two types of this request. One, the order is a pre-arranged copy job with the facility and/or location due to special circumstances and/or equipment needs. Two, W.C.A.B (Worker's Compensation Appeals Board) orders. These orders do not require a subpoena or authorization. The records we are attempting to obtain are public record and therefore are available upon order.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > SERVE ONLY/ PERSONAL APPEARANCE
text: These subpoenas will be specified on the header of the work order. They will use the wording Personal Appearance and Things or Trial. These subpoenas are different as they do not require any follow up calls. Once served the order will be returned to our department and should immediately be forwarded to the Assistant Supervisor/Team Lead for handling.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > AFFIDAVITS
text: An affidavit is a written declaration that the information provided is sworn to be true. The affidavit will always identify what records were released, to whom they belong to, and from where they are being released from. It is the legal safeguard for stating "this is all we have". Any Nevada client requires that every affidavit obtained be notarized as this is their state law.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > DEFINITIONS
text:
ABSTRACT-Some locations will make doctors notes, emergency room records, and test results available, instead of an entire medical chart that includes nurse's notes, etc. Usually this is done at hospitals where charts can be large.

ADDRESS SERVED- The address where a subpoena or authorization has been served via mail, fax or in person by agent.

ADJUSTER- A designated party who reviews your claim to determine action up to and including financial compensation.

ATTORNEY- A person who is hired or appointed to represent a party in a lawsuit. An individual who orders the request.

AFFIDAVIT OF CUSTODIAN OF RECORDS- Affidavit signed by custodian when records, bills, films, etc. are obtained at a location.

AFFIDAVIT OF NO RECORDS- Affidavit that states a location we have served has no records on the subject we have requested. (Also known as an ANR or CNR)

AFFIDAVIT OF SERVICE- Affidavit that verifies an agent we have served a subpoena or authorization to a location. (California orders)

A.K.A.- "Also Known As"

APPLICANT- A person who applied for Worker's Compensation Benefits.

APPLICANT COUNSEL- Counsel for Plaintiff, and/or additional counsel for the defense.

ARBITRATOR- A person approved by the state to act as the judge during Arbitration.

ARBITRATION- A mini trial; has all the power of a trial without a jury. A tool used by the court in an attempt to settle cases. Note: Discovery Cut Off is 15 days prior to the date of the arbitration. If the depo date is not set at least 15 days prior to the date set for arbitration, the attorney must subpoena records to the arbitration.

AUTHORIZATION- Document signed by the patient allowing the release of his/her records by the location. (Also could be signed by a guardian, parent, or person with a power of attorney)

CUSTODIAN (of records) - Individual responsible for the release of any type of records.

DATE OF SERVICE- The date a subpoena or authorization is served. Or the date of service for a patient (date of injury or treatment)

DAYS AND HOURS- The days and hours that our agent will be scheduled to go to the location (serve, scan, etc.)

DEFENDANT- The individual or business that is being sued. The side that our client represents.

DISCOVERY- Pre-trial method for obtaining facts and information about the case from the other party or witnesses. Discovery is the process used by attorneys to prepare for trial (up to 30 days before trial) or arbitration (up to 15 days before arbitration). Discovery includes depositions, interrogations, subpoenas, production of documents/things, obtaining medical and business records, etc.

DISCOVERY CUT OFF- The time in which discovery must stop.

D.O.B. - Date of birth of the claimant/patient.

D.O.S. - Date of service. The date in which services were rendered for the claimant/patient.

DUE DATE- The date that the records are due in our client's office. (This is usually the same as the depo date)

DUE DILIGENCE- Everything we did to get records. (Our statuses in Wincopy notates all of our due diligence)

EXECUTORSHIP PAPERS- Documents that indicate the person(s) authorized to obtain information on a deceased claimant.

FACILITY- The hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility where the patient's records are located and can be obtained.

FEES- A location can charge us a fee to obtain records, films, photos, etc.

HAND NOTICE- Plaintiff counsel is notices by hand/in person rather than by mail.

HIPAA- Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. These laws were enacted, April 2003, to develop standards and requirements for maintenance and transmission of health information and identifies individual patients.

HTTPS- Hypertext Protocol Secure. A protocol for secure connections on the Internet using SSL technology.

NOTICE OF CONSUMER- A document that notifies the records subject that his/her records are being sought.

HOUSE OR IN-HOUSE COUNSEL- A Insurance Company or Business's attorney or law firm which exclusively represents that business.

I.M.E. - Independent Medical Examiner

IN PRO PER- (Ion propriety persona) Someone who represents himself as his/her own attorney in a lawsuit as opposed to hiring or having an attorney appointed to represent him/her. The person is said to be "In Pro Per".

INTERROGATORIES- List of questions sent to the record subject requesting medical providers, places of employment, any insurance claim carriers or other questions that will help with the discovery process. (These normally ask for name, aka, and date of birth)

LOCATION- The facility we will be contacting when obtaining records and/or films. Also known as provider. The location is where our agents serve, scan records, etc.

LETTER OF REPRESENTATION- Letter advising provider that A.B.I. Document Support Services is the authorized representative for agent/adjuster/attorney.

MEDICAL LIEN: The right of a hospital, doctor or health care provider to assert an interest in personal injury recoveries to the extent of the cost of the treatment or service provided. NOTE: Health care providers cannot delay release of records pursuant to a request because they do not have a lien signed. See Code.

MOTION TO COMPEL- A document from the court requiring the location/facility to release records.

MOTION TO QUASH- A legal document filed with the court demanding all work be stopped immediately on every location listed on the motion. There will be a hearing date listed on the motion at which time all parties will go before the judge and present their case as to why or why not the records should or should not be made available to copy.

NEXT OF KIN- The person in a family to be successor after a family member has been Diseased. (The wife is deceased; her husband would be the successor.)

NON-CONSUMER- Records of property or things that are not owned by an individual or group.

OBJECTION- When one does not agree that records should be released either because the request is too broad or the location's records are not pertinent to the case.

ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE- A document from the court requiring the C/R to appear before the judge and give good cause as to why they did not comply with the subpoena or other types of court requests.

PATIENT- An individual awaiting or under medical care and treatment.

PERSONAL APPEARANCE SUBPOENA- A subpoena that requires a person to either appear at court with or without records, or in lieu of an appearance, mail the records directly to the court.

PITCHESS MOTION- In order to obtain personnel records of any peace officer in California, a "Pitches" motion is require to be filed with the court and granted by a judge in order to obtain the records.

PLAINTIFF- The individual or business that has made the claim/law suit.

POWER OF ATTORNEY- A legal authorization to act as the legal agent of another person.

PROOF OF SERVICE- (By mail or Hand Served) A signed and dated statement or form in which a person verifies that a specific document was mailed or delivered to a specific party. Evidence that he/she has made service on the person who has to be served with the subpoena or summons and complaint.

PROVIDER- Custodian of the requested records, such as a hospital, clinic, etc.

PUBLIC RECORDS- An order type where we do not need a subpoena or an authorization to obtain records. .or the records from this location are made available to the public. (Example: when we have orders to the Workers' Compensation Appeal Board (W.C.A.B.)

Q.M.E. - Qualified Medical Examiner (used in Workers Compensation Cases)

RESPONDENT- A person responding to the complaint.

SANCTIONS- Fines and or penalties up to and including imprisonment that can be brought against parties that hinder the production of records.

STATUS- Ongoing history of contact with the location we are requesting records from.

SUBPOENA DUCES TECUM (SDT) - a writ commanding a person to produce in court certain designated documents or evidence (Duces Tecum – Latin for Records)

SUBPOENAING PARTY- The party or person who is causing the subpoena to be issued.

SUBSTITUTION OF ATTORNEY- When one attorney or their client determines a new attorney may be able to represent the client better.

SUMMONS- A document notifying a party or parties they are being sued and the time frame in which they must respond to the court with their version with regards to the action being brought against them.

TRIAL- The examination before a judicial tribunal of the facts put in issue in a cause, often including issues of the law as well as those of fact.

WET SIGNATURE- The original blue ink signature on the Subpoena being provided after requested by a custodian of records (AKA: Original Signature from Attorney)

WITNESS- A person who has information about the subject matter of a lawsuit, but who is not a party (plaintiff or defendant) involved in the lawsuit.

WORKERS' COMPENSATION- Legally mandated provisions for awards to an employee or their dependents in case of employment related accidents or diseases.

WORKERS' COMPENSATION APPEALS BOARD (WCAB) - The legal authority in California which handles a workers disputed claim to compensation for work related injury.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > HIPAA LAW
text: The HIPAA Privacy Rule establishes standards to protect an individual's medical records and other personal health information. The rule requires safeguards and sets limits and conditions on the uses and disclosures that could be made of such information without patient authorization. This gives the individual rights over their own health information. This Privacy Rule is located at 45 CFR part 160 ad subparts A and E Part 164.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > DISCOVERY LAW
text:
A pre-trial procedure in a lawsuit in which each party can obtain evidence from the other party or parties. This

disclosure is called "Discovery" which can come in 3 forms; written discovery, document production and depositions.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > INTERROGATORIES
text:
To interrogate a witness the attorney would request a questionnaire to be completed, this form will be

conducted under oath.

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > REQUESTS FOR PRODUCTION
text:
A legal request for documents, electronically stored information or other tangible items made in the course of

litigation. (Under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 34)

topic_path: 2. Hartford Region – Frequently Asked Questions > DEPOSITIONS
text:
This is the process of giving sworn evidence. A deposition is the taking of an oral statement of a witness under

oath, before trial. The purpose of discovery is to make the parties aware of the evidence that may be presented at

trial.

topic_path: 1. Liberty Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.10 Call Flow Helpful Tips
text:
Pre Call:

1. Review the order
a. Status history and uploaded documents.
i. If follow up, review original to ensure we did not receive what is being requested on the follow up or alt. contact information (notes or records received)
b. Review the type of records requested.
i. If Subpoena, affidavit
ii. If Texas Civil Subpoena, DWQs
c. Subpoena Phrase for specific claim, DOS, etc.
d. Days request has been open.
e. If a payment has been issued, when, and has it been cashed.
f. Any numbers, emails, faxes we have tried and have been successful receiving a response.
g. The number of attempts have we made.
h. Any notices that have or have not been sent.
2. Know your objective
a. Is this a status check
b. Confirmation of receipt of request
c. Confirmation of receipt of payment
d. Escalation delay
e. Firm completion date
3. Prepare your ask
a. "Can you confirm when the records will be completed?"
b. "What is preventing the release of records at this time?
c. "What is the exact turnaround time from today?"
4. Documentation ready
a. Have all information readily available to reduce time spent on the call

During Call:

1. Strong opening
a. "Hello, this is (NAME) calling from ABI Document Support Services regarding a records request for (RECORD TYPES). Are you the best point of contact for these records or you able to provide the best point of contact for these records?"

***Confident and friendly tone = faster cooperation***

2. Verify key milestones – Ask clearly – if Applicable
a. Did you receive the request? (Confirm WO)
b. Is it valid and complete to your facility's policy?
c. Is the phone, fax, email, address we have on file correct?
d. Are fees required?
e. Has the request been processed? (Confirm WO and Record Types)
f. If not, where is it in the queue?
g. What is the expected completion date?
h. Can you send to me directly to ensure quicker processing?
i. West Region - California location addresses: Can we pay and pick up? Can we pick up? Can we Copy?
j. Central Region - Texas location addresses: Can we pay and pick up? Can we pick up? Can we Copy?

***Never hang up without a date or clear next step***

3. Handle delays with urgency
a. "Its in process"  "What is the estimated completion date?"
b. "Were behind"  "What is the earliest realistic release date?"
c. "We don't have it"  "Can I resend it while I have you on the call?

***Push politely (assertive, yet professional). Always obtain a timeline. Use prior conversations and dates to your advantage***

4. Confirm before ending
a. "Just to confirm, (XYZ) will be completed by __ and sent via __?"
5. Professional close
a. "Thank you for your assistance. We will follow up on __ if no response has been received."

Post Call:

1. Detailed notes – Aka Audit Criteria (Avoid $ amounts, specific emails, faxes, names, dates, etc. and other WOs not pertaining to that record subject)
a. Name of custodian
b. Direct phone/fax/email
c. Record types (affidavit/DWQ if required)
d. Exact status
e. Any barriers
2. Ask teammates or leadership if they have any helpful information on this facility

***Future you, teammates, client, CR, etc should not need to guess what your notes mean***

3. Immediate action items
a. Resend request? (Ensure all required items are included: Auth, Subpoena, LOR, etc.)
b. Send Notice?
c. Follow up internally?
d. Send order to CR? (Ensure we do not already have in Attachments, Print Single Models, or other orders where we have received records)

Urgency mindset:

1. Every call ends with a date
2. Every delay gets a valid reason
3. Every note tells a story of the call
4. Everything is done 100% before moving on to next order

display_title: 1.13 Client Relations – Record Retrieval and Record Retrieval – Client Relations
header: 1.13 Client Relations – Record Retrieval and Record Retrieval – Client Relations
text:
Client Relations and Customer Service are interchangeable terms for the department that handles our Clients directly and their concerns. Any time that we need more information or need to report an issue that we've run into that we cannot fix in our own department, we notify Client Relations for further review/ assistance.

The flow of information must be passed within the Retrieval and Client Relations departments. The Custodian/ Facility will never speak to Client Relations directly just as Retrieval will never speak to the Client directly. In order for the communication to stay open both Retrieval and Client Relations must relay the information being requested from the Custodian/ Facility and the Client.

There are only certain occasions where the Custodian/ Facility and the Client will get in contact with each other. Such as, the Custodian/ Facility may want more details on the case (which ABI does not have), to clarify the information being requested on the subpoena/ authorization or if they refuse to speak with ABI regarding a concern. Our Client may also contact the Facility directly if they are being non-compliant and we request for them to intervene.

topic_path: 1. Liberty Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.14 Email Etiquette for Professional Workplaces
text:
With the sheer volume of emails that we read and write each day, we may be more prone to making errors and those errors can have professional consequences. Here are important tips you need to know when writing an email in your professional environment.

Include a clear, direct subject line. People often decide whether to open an email based on the subject line. Good subject lines give the reader a preview of what the email is about.

Begin each email with a greeting: No matter how pressed for time you are, a simple greeting such as "Hi," "Hello," or "Dear" is good etiquette. Otherwise, if you launch into your email without a greeting or introduction you run the risk of seeming impolite or impatient.

End emails in a friendly way: Use ending such as "Best wishes" or "Have a great day". Even if you use the same ending with everyone, it ends the email in a warm and positive way.

Think twice before hitting Reply All. No one wants to read emails from 20 people that have nothing to do with them. Refrain from hitting Reply All unless you really think everyone on the list needs to receive the email.

Include a signature block. Provide your reader with some information about you, such as your full name, title, the organization name, and your contact information, including a phone number. Use the same font, type size, and color as the rest of the email.

Be cautious with humour. Humour can easily get lost in translation without the right tone or facial expressions. In a professional exchange, it is better to leave humour out of emails unless you know the recipient well.

Proofread every message. Ensure you are using correct spelling and proper grammar. Your mistakes will be noticed by the recipients and you may be judged for making them. Do not rely on spell-checkers. Read and reread your email, preferably aloud, before sending it.

Add the email address last. This prevents you from sending an email accidentally before you have finished writing and proofing the message. Even when you are replying to a message, it's a good precaution to delete the recipient's address and insert it only when you are sure the message is ready to be sent.

Double-check that you have selected the correct recipient. Pay careful attention when typing a name on the email's "To" line. It is easy to select the wrong name and this could cause a breach of privacy, embarrassment, or wasted time.

Keep your fonts classic. The ideal font is Arial, size 12 in black. Your emails should be easy for other people to read.

Keep tabs on your tone. Tone is easy to misconstrue without the context from vocal cues and facial expressions. It's easy to appear more abrupt than you intended. Avoid using negative words ("failure," "wrong," "neglected"), and use "please" and "thank you." To avoid misunderstandings, read your message out loud before sending.

Nothing is confidential--so write accordingly. A basic guideline is to assume that others will see what you write. Don't write anything that would be ruinous to you or hurtful to others. After all, work email is owned by your organization and email is easy to forward.

Use threads: if you get a message from someone and you are going to respond, don't send a new message, simply hit the reply option on your email, this keeps the original subject line with "Re:" in front of it.

Protect addresses: If you are sending out an email to a large private list use BCC: (blind carbon copy), don't use CC: (carbon copy) to protect the addresses of the recipients.

Be concise: Get to the point of your email as quickly as possible, but don't leave out important details that will help your recipient answer your query.

Do not use all CAPS in your emails: This is perceived as yelling in the digital world. If you need to emphasize something, use bold or italics on the points you want to emphasize.

If you are sending an email with an attachment, make mention of it in the body of the email: Write in the email that you are sending an attachment so that the reader knows there is more to the email than just the text.

Use an Auto-responder: When you're away from the office and not available for an extended time, set an auto-responder to automatically reply to emails. Include the email of another colleague for emergencies. This lets people know when to expect a response and who to contact if a response is required sooner.

Don't send an email when you are emotional or angry. Wait for 24 hours before writing your response or hitting send.

topic_path: 1. Liberty Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.20 Non-Compliance Process
text:
Question

What is the Liberty Region process for marking an order non-compliant?

Procedure

A facility is considered "non-compliant" when the due/ deposition date has passed. The facility may have stated that records have been in process for weeks without a valid explanation or if you have not had any valid contact with the facility. Ensure that the below due diligence has been applied and followed.

1. Read all the notes for important/maybe different contact info.
2. Attempt all numbers in profile (even if it's not for the record type you are following up for)
3. Attempt all options, not just for the dept. for the record type we are following up for.
4. Ask for a manager!
a. If manager is not available.
i. When will they be in?
ii. Do they have a direct number, email, and fax?
iii. Who is their boss?
iv. Is the doctor available?
5. Check other orders for that facility for alt. contact info.
6. Google for alt. contact (send a fax/email on top of making phone calls to the facility)
7. Check for duplicates
8. Send appropriate non-compliant notices. (Follow the SOPs)

When leaving messages, you must express the upmost urgency. Advise how many calls we have made, the due date, the non-compliance notices we have sent, the lack of response, if a response is not received the client may petition a Motion to Compel, as well as request an immediate call back from the manager that day!

*You must note ALL of your efforts*

topic_path: 1. Liberty Region – Highlights and Exceptions > 1.25 Solcom Fix - QC Codes
text:
When handing the fix basket, you should be reviewing the notes in Solcom not Wincopy to identify why it was returned. There will be 1 of 2 things listed for your return.

1. There should be a detailed description from QC or Lead indicating what is needed.
2. If no detailed description, there should be a QC# code. Each number stands for something.

QC1- Order is already closed and billed. Something was uploaded to the order after it was closed. You need to see what was uploaded and identify if you need to create a follow up and have the items moved to the follow up order, or verify if they are duplicate and let us know if we need to disregard.

QC2- The order is missing a status letter for your closeout, or its missing an affidavit of records or of no records. You will need to identify which one based on how it was closed and what's present and not present in Solcom.

QC3- Records are not showing in Solcom, therefore you need to re-upload them. This could be of system issues, or may have dropped them incorrectly.

QC4- You need to verify records are correct. This means either the name, date of birth, and or facility name does not match what the client provided on the order. You need to verify if they are correct. If they are you need to enter a note for QC that its ok to process records as you verified they are correct.

QC5- The incorrect status letter format was uploaded, wrong affidavit, or you need a status letter because the custodian filled out the affidavit incorrectly, meaning they signed it on the wrong spot, or they marked something was not provided when in fact it was provided.

QC6- There is an invoice in Solcom on this order showing as unpaid. You need to verify if it needs to be paid and move forward with the process of issuing payment. Once payment is issued your leads can move the order back to QC.

topic_path: 2. Liberty Region – Frequently Asked Questions > 2.2 Central - Follow Up Orders
text:
Question

What are follow up orders and how should they be handled?

Follow ups are orders that are created from original orders. Follow ups may be created by Client Relations or Clerical Support to either obtain records that were not originally provided or to challenge a CNR. Follow ups from Client Relations need more diligence as we either, already received records but maybe missing some necessary documents or if the client has provided proof that records do exist after we already obtained a CNR. Follow ups from Clerical Support are orders that you request personally such as a Bcopy, Xcopy or for the signed affidavit.

· Bcopy: Specifically created for billing records

· Xcopy: Specifically created for digital imaging ONLY, if they exist at the facility

· Follow up for missing records: Created by Client Relations as the Client believes not all records were provided or if specific information is missing

· Follow up for missing Affidavit of Custodian of Records: Created by Clerical Support to continue following up for the missing affidavit as records were previously provided without

· Follow up to challenge CNR: Created by Client Relations if the Client provides some form of proof that records exist or if they provide additional information that may help the facility locate records

· Follow up for additional fees: Created by your Lead or Supervisor as records were already received and processed but we failed to pay the fees before we closed the order. These should be sent to your Lead or Supervisor to review and have fees issued and order closed

*** If an order is a M/B/X or M/X and an invoice or breakdown for the xrays is received, a follow up order will need to be requested and marked as high importance for an Xcopy as Xrays must be their own order. Email is TexusFU@abidss.com ***
