text:
- For RED or SAC routes, please email Kaipo Harck (Field Supervisor) and Danielle Luna (Field Lead)
- For FULL or LA routes, please email Eric Kim (Field Supervisor) and Brandon Ginchereau (Field Lead)

If records are ready to be picked up or copied, schedule accordingly. Make sure you ask all of the questions below as

your driver does not have DocPro to verify information:

• Are we picking up or copying? (THIS MAKES A BIG DIFFERENCE IN THE DRIVER'S TRIP)
- If copy, verify how many inches so that your driver has an idea on how long it will take

(Generally, 1 inch can take anywhere from 20-30 minutes)

• What are the days and hours our driver can go? (Ex: M-F 8-12/1-5; Tues & Thurs 8-12; Fridays Only 8-5)

-If a specific appointment necessary, if so follow the below instructions (Ex: Monday, April 6th @ 10am

• If the order is requesting billing records, Is billing included?

-If yes, make sure to list it (Ex: medical and billing records)

-If no, the facility needs to provide an explanation on the Affidavit as to why they do not have billing or

where it can be obtained from

• If the order is requesting Xrays, does their office perform any imaging in-house?

-If no, use the VPU/VTC status with "NO FILMS"

text:
Follow Up's are orders created from an original order by Client Relations or Clerical Support when something

additional is needed, records are missing or to challenge a facility.

Follow Ups from Client Relations need more diligence as we already received records but may be missing some

necessary documents or dates of service. Client Relations Follow Ups are also created if the Client has provided

proof that records DO exist after a CNR was already obtained.

Follow ups from Clerical Support are orders that you request personally or will be requested from Quality Control(QC)

due to documents missing when records are being processed.

• Bcopy: Specifically created for billing records
• Xcopy: Specifically created for digital imaging ONLY, if they exist at the facility
• Follow up for missing records: Created by Client Relations as the Client believes not all records were provided or if

specific information is missing

• Follow up for missing Affidavit of Custodian of Records: Created by Clerical Support to continue following up for the

missing affidavit as records were previously provided without

• Follow up to challenge CNR: Created by Client Relations if the Client provides some form of proof that records exist or if

they provide additional information that may help the facility locate records

• Follow up for additional fees: Created by your Lead or Supervisor as records were already received and processed but

we failed to pay the fees before we closed the order

** Please note, when calling on a Follow Up order these SHOULD NOT be addressed the same as a new

order. Meaning we should be specifying that records were previously received but something is missing

or that a CNR was previously received but the Client has provided proof **

informed that a CNR would be provided.

When a facility informs you that a CNR will be sent to us, update the order using

If we still have not received the CNR by the fourth attempt, the order can be closed

with the "AFFIDAVIT-NO RECORDS-FACILITY 4TH VERBAL"as a Status Letter.

This way the order is no longer delayed and we have done our diligence to obtain

the CNR. In the event the CNR is received at a later time, a follow up will be created

to process.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > CLIENT APPROVAL RULE
text:
Most requests automatically come with a processing fee. The average processing fee is $15, which is dropped off

at the same time our rep serves the request or will be submitted if the request is mailed. Some smaller offices may

charge anywhere from $25-$50. However, always request an invoice that way we can mail the check along with a

copy. This assists with pairing the correct fees to the correct order.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > PAYING BY CHECK
text:
When an invoice has been received, upload it to Import using the label "_rrchk" (Ex: 1234567-89_rrchk).

Your status will be "INVOICE-RECEIVED" and your Trigger "SENT-CHECKS". Once the check has been cut and

mailed, the order will be sent back to your basket for you to continue following up.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > PAYING BY CREDIT CARD
text:
If you receive an invoice that needs to be paid by Credit Card, you will still need to upload a copy of the invoice to

Import (Ex: 1234567-89_rrchk). Instead of sending the order to the Check Desk, the order will stay with you but an

email needs to be sent in order for payment to be completed.

Email the link/ invoice received to Supportids@abidss.com, payment should be completed before end of day. You will

not Trigger this order but instead, you will add a "SOLCOM-RETREIVAL NOTE" stating "Emailed SupportIDS".

**In the event that you need to verify if a check has cleared, to void a check or need a copy of a

cleared check - email the accounting at spchecksclearedthebank@abidss.com and CC the Retrieval Leads**

**Any invoices over $250 need approval from our client. We do this by using the

status "INVOICE/PAGECOUNT-APPROVAL NEEDED", fill out the fields

accordingly, then Trigger using "SENT-ESCALATE REVIEW" **

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DOCUMENT RETRIEVAL PROCEDURES
5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > XRAY BREAKDOWN
text:
An Xray breakdown is a list of exams that were taken of the patient. The breakdown lists what exams were taken, the

film count and the cost of obtaining the images. Anytime a facility has images available we need to obtain a

breakdown first, as we have to get approval from our Client before paying. Breakdowns come in various formats so

always keep an eye out when receiving them as you may mistake them for an invoice or billing records.

Ex:

If a breakdown is received, upload it to Import using label "_rrcorr". Your status will be "FILM - BREAKDOWN

AVAILABLE", this status does not specify that a breakdown has already received because we still need additional

time for internal processing. Your Trigger will be "SENT-XRAY/FILM DESK".

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > NO BREAKDOWN
text:
Some facilities may not provide breakdowns at all and charge a flat fee for their cds however, they may still provide

an invoice. The invoice still needs to follow the Client Approval Rule, meaning anything $250 and over will need to

be approved (follow Client Approval Rule process, see age 59).

To process the No Breakdown, upload the invoice to Import using label "_rrchk", then we must notify the Client using

the “FILM-NO BREAKDOWN” status. Your Trigger will be "SENT-CHECKS".

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > NON-COMPLIANCE “RULE OF THUMB”
text:
A facility is considered “non-compliant” when the due/ deposition date has passed. The facility may have stated that records have been in

process for weeks without a valid explanation or if you have not had any valid contact with the facility. On an order that was just served,

the procedure is to follow up for 2-3 weeks and then send a Second Notice. If records/correspondence still have not been obtained,

continue to follow up for another 2 weeks and if nothing, then send a Final Notice. After the Final Notice you want to follow up one at

least one last time before sending it to Client Relations as “Non-Compliant”.

***NOTE**** You need to be as detailed as possible and show your efforts. Request to speak to a supervisor or manager if you cannot

reach the main custodian. Google other methods of contact such as an email, fax or a different phone number. Any gaps in your statuses

may result in the order coming back for you to continue following up.

text:

the order must be sent to Client Relations.

Client Relations will update the Client and to give them the option of continuing following up or to close the

order until a response has been received.

Lengthy delay orders can be statused every 15 days unlike normal orders where an update is needed every

forward it to Client Relations using "NON COMPLIANCE-HOLD FOR CLIENT RESPONSE". Your Trigger will

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > AUTHORIZATION REJECTIONS
text:
An authorization can be rejected for more multiple reasons such as missing information, invalid format, etc. When a

rejection is received or the facility verbally informs you that the authorization is rejected, you must first review the

authorization yourself to confirm what they are stating, is in fact true. The authorization can be found under the

"Attachments".

•

If their rejection is incorrect - you will push back, proceed to assist and get the order back on track

•

If their rejection is valid - you will choose the status that fits best and send the order to Client Relations by

Triggering "Sent-Escalate Review". That order will sit in Client Relations for 10 days awaiting for a response

from the Client.

Multiple Rejections

In the event that the authorization is rejected for multiple reasons, you can choose the status that fits the main reason,

then amend and add the other rejection reasons manually.

Client Provided Amended Authorization

When the Client provides the amend authorization, the request will need to be resubmitted. Contact the facility to

confirm if you can fax or email a copy of the request with the amended authorization instead of having to reserve.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > HIPAA COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST - AUTHORIZATION
text:
INFORMATION 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(i) A description of the information to be disclosed that identifies the

information in a specific and meaningful fashion.

DISCLOSING ENTITY 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(ii) The name or other specific identification of the

person(s), or class of persons, authorized to make the disclosure.

RECIPIENT 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(iii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or

class of persons, to whom the covered entity may make the requested disclosure.

PURPOSE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(iv) A description of each purpose of the requested use or

disclosure. The statement “at the request of the individual” is a sufficient description of the

purpose when an individual initiates the authorization an does not, or elects not to, provide a

statement of the purpose.

EXPIRATION DATE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(v) An expiration date or an expiration event that relates

to the use or disclosure.

SIGNATURE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(1)(vi) Signature of the individual and date. A copy of a signature

is sufficient if the document states “a copy shall be considered as original”.

RIGHT TO REVOKE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(2)(i) The exceptions to the right to revoke and a description

of how the individual may revoke the authorization.

NO CONDITIONS 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(2)(ii) The covered entity may not condition treatment,

payment, enrollment or eligibility for benefits on whether the individual signs the authorization.

POTENTIAL FOR REDISCLOSURE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(2)(iii) The potential for information disclosed

pursuant to the authorization to be subject to redisclosure by the recipient and no longer protected.

PLAIN LANGUAGE 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(3) Authorization is written in plain language.

COPY TO INDIVIDUAL 45 CFR 164.508 (c)(4) If a covered entity seeks an authorization from an

individual for use or disclosure of protected health information, the covered entity must provide

the individual with a copy of the signed authorization. This is not applicable to copy services.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DEFINITIONS
text:
ABSTRACT-Some locations will make doctors notes, emergency room records, and test results available, instead of an

entire medical chart that includes nurse’s notes, etc. Usually this is done at hospitals where charts can be large.

ADDRESS SERVED- The address where a subpoena or authorization has been served via mail, fax or in person by agent.

ADJUSTER- A designated party who reviews your claim to determine action up to and including financial compensation.

ATTORNEY- A person who is hired or appointed to represent a party in a lawsuit. An individual who orders the request.

AFFIDAVIT OF CUSTODIAN OF RECORDS- Affidavit signed by custodian when records, bills, films, etc. are obtained at a

location.

AFFIDAVIT OF NO RECORDS- Affidavit that states a location we have served has no records on the subject we have

requested. (Also known as an ANR or CNR)

AFFIDAVIT OF SERVICE- Affidavit that verifies an agent we have served a subpoena or authorization to a location.

(California orders)

A.K.A.- “Also Known As”

APPLICANT- A person who applied for Worker’s Compensation Benefits.

APPLICANT COUNSEL- Counsel for Plaintiff, and/or additional counsel for the defense.

ARBITRATOR- A person approved by the state to act as the judge during Arbitration.

ARBITRATION- A mini trial; has all the power of a trial without a jury. A tool used by the court in an attempt to settle

cases. Note: Discovery Cut Off is 15 days prior to the date of the arbitration. If the depo date is not set at least 15 days

prior to the date set for arbitration, the attorney must subpoena records to the arbitration.

AUTHORIZATION- Document signed by the patient allowing the release of his/her records by the location. (Also could

be signed by a guardian, parent, or person with a power of attorney)

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DEFINITIONS
text:
BILLING DEPARTMENT- The department/custodian of billing records for a claimant/patient.

BUSINESS OFFICE- The department/custodian of billing records of a claimant/patient.

CASE SETTLED- When a case settled you must discontinue work on that order. All case settled orders are be pulled and

closed out within 48 hours to ensure we receive payment.

CIVIL LAW- Law’s which nation, state or city enacts to protect the privacy of all individuals. Generally, any law that is not

criminal. Civil Law pertains to non-criminal matters.

CLAIM- To demand for explanation and/or to claim loss that requires a response in writing up to financial reimbursement.

CLAIMANT- Individual such as the patient who is the subject of the records request.

CLAIM/CASE NUMBER- A number of ID provided by the client for tracking the request. For example, an insurance agent

or adjuster may want to identify records by a specific policy or claim number.

CLAUSE- All records being requested. Including: Medical, Billing, Films, Insurance, School, Prescription/Pharmacy, etc.

Specific information can also be located in the clause, such as a treating doctor, policy number, etc.

CLIENT- The party requesting records on the claimant/patient (Insurance Company, Law Firm).

COMPLAINT- A document, that follows a Summons, (one page or more) which represents the case name, the case

number, court, and an explanation as to why you are being sued. (Rarely do you have a summons without a complaint.)

CONSUMER- Any person whose records are being sought. This could be medical, professional, or personal.

COPIES- The number of copies of a record that are being requested by the client.

COURT ORDER- A demand by the court.

CRIMINAL LAW- Pertaining to crimes and penal justice.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DEFINITIONS
text:
CUSTODIAN (of records) - Individual responsible for the release of any type of records.

DATE OF SERVICE- The date a subpoena or authorization is served. Or the date of service for a patient (date of injury or

treatment)

DAYS AND HOURS- The days and hours that our agent will be scheduled to go to the location (serve, scan, etc.)

DEFENDANT- The individual or business that is being sued. The side that our client represents.

DISCOVERY- Pre-trial method for obtaining facts and information about the case from the other party or witnesses.

Discovery is the process used by attorneys to prepare for trial (up to 30 days before trial) or arbitration (up to 15 days

before arbitration). Discovery includes depositions, interrogations, subpoenas, production of documents/things, obtain-

ing medical and business records, etc.

DISCOVERY CUT OFF- The time in which discovery must stop.

D.O.B. - Date of birth of the claimant/patient.

D.O.S. - Date of service. The date in which services were rendered for the claimant/patient.

DUE DATE- The date that the records are due in our client’s office. (This is usually the same as the depo date)

DUE DILIGENCE- Everything we did to get records. (Our statuses in Wincopy notates all of our due diligence)

EXECUTORSHIP PAPERS- Documents that indicate the person(s) authorized to obtain information on a deceased claim-

ant.

FACILITY- The hospital, clinic, or healthcare facility where the patient’s records are located and can be obtained.

FEES- A location can charge us a fee to obtain records, films, photos, etc.

HAND NOTICE- Plaintiff counsel is notices by hand/in person rather than by mail.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DEFINITIONS
text:
HIPAA- Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. These laws were enacted, April 2003, to develop standards

and requirements for maintenance and transmission of health information and identifies individual patients.

HTTPS- Hypertext Protocol Secure. A protocol for secure connections on the Internet using SSL technology.

NOTICE OF CONSUMER- A document that notifies the records subject that his/her records are being sought.

HOUSE OR IN-HOUSE COUNSEL- A Insurance Company or Business’s attorney or law firm which exclusively represents

that business.

I.M.E. - Independent Medical Examiner

IN PRO PER- (Ion propriety persona) Someone who represents himself as his/her own attorney in a lawsuit as opposed

to hiring or having an attorney appointed to represent him/her. The person is said to be “In Pro Per”.

INTERROGATORIES- List of questions sent to the record subject requesting medical providers, places of employment,

any insurance claim carriers or other questions that will help with the discovery process. (These normally ask for name,

aka, and date of birth)

LOCATION- The facility we will be contacting when obtaining records and/or films. Also known as provider. The location

is where our agents serve, scan records, etc.

LETTER OF REPRESENTATION- Letter advising provider that A.B.I. Document Support Services is the authorized repre-

sentative for agent/adjuster/attorney.

MEDICAL LIEN: The right of a hospital, doctor or health care provider to assert an interest in personal injury recoveries

to the extent of the cost of the treatment or service provided. NOTE: Health care providers cannot delay release of

records pursuant to a request because they do not have a lien signed. See Code.

MOTION TO COMPEL- A document from the court requiring the location/facility to release records.

MOTION TO QUASH- A legal document filed with the court demanding all work be stopped immediately on every loca-

tion listed on the motion. There will be a hearing date listed on the motion at which time all parties will go before the

judge and present their case as to why or why not the records should or should not be made available to copy.

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DEFINITIONS
text:
NEXT OF KIN- The person in a family to be successor after a family member has been Diseased. (The wife is deceased;

her husband would be the successor.)

NON-CONSUMER- Records of property or things that are not owned by an individual or group.

OBJECTION- When one does not agree that records should be released either because the request is too broad or the

location’s records are not pertinent to the case.

ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE- A document from the court requiring the C/R to appear before the judge and give good

cause as to why they did not comply with the subpoena or other types of court requests.

PATIENT- An individual awaiting or under medical care and treatment.

PERSONAL APPEARANCE SUBPOENA- A subpoena that requires a person to either appear at court with or without

records, or in lieu of an appearance, mail the records directly to the court.

PITCHESS MOTION- In order to obtain personnel records of any peace officer in California, a “Pitches” motion is require

to be filed with the court and granted by a judge in order to obtain the records.

PLAINTIFF- The individual or business that has made the claim/law suit.

POWER OF ATTORNEY- A legal authorization to act as the legal agent of another person.

PROOF OF SERVICE- (By mail or Hand Served) A signed and dated statement or form in which a person verifies that a

specific document was mailed or delivered to a specific party. Evidence that he/she has made service on the person who

has to be served with the subpoena or summons and complaint.

PROVIDER- Custodian of the requested records, such as a hospital, clinic, etc.

PUBLIC RECORDS- An order type where we do not need a subpoena or an authorization to obtain records. .or the

records from this location are made available to the public. (Example: when we have orders to the Workers’ Compensa-

tion Appeal Board (W.C.A.B.)

topic_path: 5678 Winter Street Suite 1 > DEFINITIONS
text:
Q.M.E. - Qualified Medical Examiner (used in Workers Compensation Cases)

RESPONDENT- A person responding to the complaint.

SANCTIONS- Fines and or penalties up to and including imprisonment that can be brought against parties that hinder

the production of records.

STATUS- Ongoing history of contact with the location we are requesting records from.

SUBPOENA DUCES TECUM (SDT) - a writ commanding a person to produce in court certain designated documents or

evidence (Duces Tecum – Latin for Records)

SUBPOENAING PARTY- The party or person who is causing the subpoena to be issued.

SUBSTITUTION OF ATTORNEY- When one attorney or their client determines a new attorney may be able to represent

the client better.

SUMMONS- A document notifying a party or parties they are being sued and the time frame in which they must respond

to the court with their version with regards to the action being brought against them.

TRIAL- The examination before a judicial tribunal of the facts put in issue in a cause, often including issues of the law as

well as those of fact.

WET SIGNATURE- The original blue ink signature on the Subpoena being provided after requested by a custodian of

records (AKA: Original Signature from Attorney)

WITNESS- A person who has information about the subject matter of a lawsuit, but who is not a party (plaintiff or defen-

dant) involved in the lawsuit.

WORKERS’ COMPENSATION- Legally mandated provisions for awards to an employee or their dependents in case of

employment related accidents or diseases.

WORKERS’ COMPENSATION APPEALS BOARD (WCAB) - The legal authority in California which handles a workers

disputed claim to compensation for work related injury.

topic_path: 2. West Region – Frequently Asked Questions > 2.1 Non-Compliance Process
text:
Question

What is the West Region process for marking an order non-compliant?

Procedure

Complete two follow-up attempts before sending the Second Notice.
Send the Second Notice together with the request.
If the deposition date has already passed and the facility cannot be reached, send the Second Notice on the first unsuccessful attempt.
If the order is approaching or has passed the due date and the facility states that the request is still in progress, send the applicable notice.
After sending the Second Notice, complete two additional follow-up attempts.
Send the Final Notice together with the request.
After the Final Notice, complete one additional follow-up attempt.
Send the order to your Supervisor before marking it non-compliant.
After Supervisor approval, update the order to:

Non-Compliant – Hold for Client Response

Add the trigger:

Sent – Non-Compliance Review

Important Note

Document every attempt, mention all email addresses and fax number where sent notice, facility response, and escalation clearly in the order notes.

Click Print.
Select Single Models.
Under Models to Show, confirm that Status is checked.
Scroll down and select STATUS-5 Final.
Click OK.
Under Select Printer, choose Adobe PDF.
Click OK.
Save the PDF using the following naming convention:

Work Order Number_abiclosout

1234567-89_abiclosout

Step 4 – Search for the New Order Form

In the Print Single Model window:

Enter NOF in the Model Name field.
Click Search.

Step 5 – Print the New Order Form

From the search results:

Select NOF.
Click Print.

Step 6 – Save the New Order Form

Save the completed New Order Form in the designated:

CCSI West Folder

Type of records being requested
Whether the change is:
Permanent
Temporary

text:

New Order Form

Email Bounce back Documentation:

When an email bounces back:

Add a Solcom retrieval note and document all relevant details in the order.
The same information must also be updated in the Viewable Status section once the next agent will work so that the client can clearly see that the email address is invalid or incorrect.

When we do not have fax and email for the facility:

When we don’t have fax and email, we will not mail the request.
We only mail the request with second/ final notice.
